name: Van Buren State Park
partner_agencies: Friends of Van Buren State Park
description: Originally inhabited by the Shawnee, the area surrounding Van Buren State Park is rich in woods and agricultural lands. The park's 296 acres offer a calm, peaceful retreat with camping, fishing, hiking, horseback riding, and picnicking opportunities that can be enjoyed year-round.
location: North of Findlay, Van Buren Township, Hancock County, Ohio
features: Hiking Trail;Bridle Trail;Pavilion;Picnic Area;Volleyball Court;Disc Golf Course;Playground;Sledding Hill;Horseshoe Pitch;Archery Range;Dog Park;Camping;Hunting Area;Fishing Area

name: Van Buren State Park Campground
description: Van Buren State Park Campground is a peaceful, quiet loop. It offers 61 sites with 50-amp electricity and water -- several perfect for tent camping. Pets are permitted on all sites. Many sites are partially shaded.
location: Within Van Buren State Park, Van Buren Township, Hancock County

name: Oakwoods Nature Preserve
description: Oakwoods Nature Preserve is a 227.5-acre outdoor complex that contains diverse habitat, nature trails, and two lakes—all anchored by the Richard S. "Doc" Phillips Discovery Center. Wetlands, woodlands, and prairie create a place for discovery and form a natural attraction full of seasonal beauty that supports wildlife, environmental education, and nature-based outdoor recreation.
features: Hiking Trail;Watercraft Access;Picnic Area;Restrooms;Parking Lot;Fishing Area

name: Litzenberg Memorial Woods
description: Litzenberg Memorial Woods contains 227.7 acres on the north side and south side of U.S. Route 224 West. Land is characterized by rolling countryside, wooded ravines, and a grand expanse of wetlands, prairie, and sky. It blends the area's rich agricultural heritage with conservation and wildlife, education and history, hiking and exploration, picnicking and play, and social gatherings and special events to create a unique destination.

name: Riverbend Recreation Area
description: Riverbend Recreation Area was the Hancock Park District's first park, which opened in 1976 for America's Bicentennial celebration. Once a Native American camp along the "big bend" of the Blanchard, the 129-acre park remains a unique habitat for wildlife. Visitors can birdwatch and take photographs as they enjoy a wide range of year-round outdoor recreation opportunities and experiences. Ample open space is available for yard games. A multi-use loop trail and nature trails weave through clearings and tree canopy, perfect for quiet dreaming and restful solitude for every season.
features: Bridle Trail;Gazebo;Volleyball Court;Disc Golf Course;Playground;Dog Park;Restrooms;Parking Lot;Fishing Area

name: Bright Conservation Area
description: Bright Conservation Area is a 29.4-acre undeveloped natural area with no support facilities. It was created to protect water quality, expand wildlife habitat, and provide natural beauty. Habitat is characterized as native wetland communities, including scrub-shrub, wet meadow, emergent herbaceous, and open water that support a variety of wildlife.

name: Lehman Conservation Area
description: Lehman Conservation Area is a 7.1-acre undeveloped natural area with no support facilities. It was created to protect water quality, expand wildlife habitat, and provide natural beauty. Habitat is characterized as early successional riparian woods and serves as a valuable feeding and staging area for migratory birds.
location: West of Riverbend Recreation Area at 16428 Township Road 208, Findlay, OH

name: Indian Green–Worden Family Conservation Area
description: Indian Green–Worden Family Conservation Area is a 27.3-acre undeveloped natural area with no support facilities. It was created to preserve the natural area along the Blanchard River, expand wildlife habitat, and provide access to the Heritage Trail via Litzenberg Memorial Woods' south unit. Habitat is characterized as mature riparian woods.
location: East of Litzenberg Memorial Woods (south unit), Findlay, OH

name: Lawrence Conservation Area
description: Lawrence Conservation Area is a 16.1-acre undeveloped natural area with no support facilities. It was created to protect water quality, expand wildlife habitat, and provide natural beauty. The Blanchard River has several mussel beds in the area that support, among other species, the federally endangered rayed bean. Visitation is by appointment only.
location: South of Township Road 236, Findlay, OH

name: Vogelsong Conservation Area
description: Vogelsong Conservation Area is a 23.6-acre undeveloped natural area with no support facilities. It was created to protect water quality, expand wildlife habitat, and provide natural beauty. Habitat is characterized as bottomland woods.
location: West of State Route 568 Bridge, Findlay, OH

name: Aeraland Recreation Area
description: Aeraland Recreation Area is a rural county park in a quiet country setting. The scenic South Branch Portage River flows through the 74.8 acres. Visitors may picnic, hike and birdwatch in relative isolation and solitude. The parkland was originally created in 1981 as a private recreational area for employees of Fostoria's Atlas Crankshaft Corporation. After the plant closed in 1999, it was donated to Washington Township trustees, then given to the Hancock Park District in 2012.

name: Blanchard River Nature Preserve
partner_agencies: Black Swamp Conservancy (BSC) — original purchaser of property in 2013; donated fee-simple title to Hancock County Park District for use as a public park. BSC has no current ownership or easement role; historical donor only. Source: blackswamp.org/property/blanchard-river-nature-preserve/ (fetched 2026-05-15).
description: With a strong emphasis on environmental preservation, visitation is limited to hiking, birdwatching, and landscape and wildlife photography along a quiet walkway to the river's edge, and boating and fishing via a primitive river access site. Blanchard River Nature Preserve provides a quiet country setting and scenic start for the 37.6-mile Blanchard River Water Trail during rare times when there is enough water for canoes and kayaks to navigate the river.

name: Blue Rock Nature Preserve
description: The 11.3-acre Blue Rock Nature Preserve is a showcase of natural succession serving as a neighborhood park and oasis and offering an escape from the hustle and bustle of life. Visitors enjoy the small wetland and woods and their inhabitants, hiking and bird watching along the .3-mile Ladybug Loop Trail, and perhaps a bench and a book.
location: Edgar Avenue and Bank Street, Findlay, OH

name: Centennial Park
description: Centennial Park is owned by the City of Findlay and managed by the Hancock Park District. The .5-acre park, while limited in its offering, integrates an outdoor fitness center with the adjacent Blanchard River Greenway Trail to create a complete exercise program.
location: Cross Avenue and East of Blanchard Street, Findlay, OH

name: Eastpoint Area
description: Eastpoint Area is owned by Hancock County and managed by the Hancock Park District. The 1-acre park affords the opportunity for fishing, canoeing and kayaking, and picnicking. It also serves as a wayside destination for resting, relaxing, and enjoying the waterfront and as the eastern terminus for the Blanchard River Greenway Trail.
location: East Main Cross Street, at Bright Road Bridge, Findlay, OH

name: Great Karg Well Historical Site
description: The Great Karg Well Historical Site is owned by the City of Findlay and managed by the Hancock Park District. The .5-acre park is the site of an historical monument honoring the Great Karg Well. As a quiet wayside destination, the park provides undeveloped access to the river for fishing. From the canoeist and kayaker perspective, it serves as a portage that gives paddlers an opportunity to rest before continuing downstream.
location: Liberty and River Street, Findlay, OH

name: River Landings
description: River Landings is owned by the City of Findlay and managed by the Hancock Park District. The 10-acre park serves as a wayside destination for rest and relaxation and presents opportunities for play and picnicking. It also serves as the western terminus for the Blanchard River Greenway Trail.

name: Waterfalls Area
description: Waterfalls Area is owned by the City of Findlay and managed by the Hancock Park District. The .5-acre park, which is located across the river from Riverside Park Waterfront, provides a soothing respite among the waterfall and majestic sycamore trees. Visitors to the Waterfalls Area may walk along the Blanchard River Greenway Trail, picnic, launch, land, and portage canoes and kayaks, and access the river for fishing.
location: 923 E Main Cross St, Findlay, OH

name: Jackson Landing
description: Jackson Landing is an undeveloped natural area along the Blanchard River Water Trail. It serves as a landing option or rest area for canoeists and kayakers paddling from Blanchard River Nature Preserve. It may also serve as an alternative starting point. Riverbend Recreation Area is located approximately 4 miles downstream from Jackson Landing.

name: Liberty Landing
description: Liberty Landing marks the beginning of a popular 9.3-mile float trip on the Blanchard River Water Trail. The trip from Liberty Landing to Blanchard Landing is scenic with frequent bends, narrow sections, and exciting riffles with no known hazards. Wildlife sightings are common. Paddlers will travel along the border of Indian Green-Worden Family Conservation Area and the south unit of Litzenberg Memorial Woods. Without stops and with strong and steady paddling, the trip takes approximately 3 hours.
location: Township Road 89, west of County Road 140, Findlay, OH

name: Blanchard Landing
description: Blanchard Landing marks the end of the 37.6-mile Blanchard River Water Trail. It also serves as a rest area or starting point for canoeists and kayakers paddling downstream to Gilboa or Ottawa in Putnam County. A popular two-day trip on the entire Blanchard River Water Trail in Hancock County – affectionately known as the Blanchard River Challenge – begins at Blanchard River Nature Preserve, involves tent camping at Riverbend Recreation Area, and ends at Blanchard Landing. Daily canoe and kayak rentals are available.
location: State Route 235, south of U.S. Route 224 West, Findlay, OH

description: Fountain Cemetery encompasses more than 38 acres between Summit and Van Buren Streets in Fostoria. Originally established as Fostoria Cemetery in 1856, renamed Fountain Cemetery in 1900 for its many fountains. Features include a Civil War monument (1919), the Lady Fountain (1895), WWI Doughboy statue (placed 1969), Veterans Memorial Chapel (built 2004, dedicated Memorial Day 2004), and a Vietnam Veteran Memorial (dedicated Nov. 11, 2009).

Open to public fishing through a cooperative agreement between the City of Findlay and the ODNR Division of Wildlife. Depths range from 20 to 28 feet (average 24 ft). Reservoir 1 has 2 miles of diked shoreline. ODNR lists this property as a public fishing area on their Find a Property page.
